sources.claim: Shuffle is Spark's mechanism for re-distributing data grouped differently across partitions; copies data across executors/machines (Spark 4.2.0 docs)
Map tasks organize data, reduce tasks aggregate; map results held in memory, sorted by target partition and written to a single file; reduce tasks read relevant sorted blocks
Operations that can cause shuffle: repartition/coalesce, ByKey ops (except counting), joins (join, cogroup)
Shuffle is expensive: disk I/O, data serialization, network I/O; spills to disk add I/O and GC; intermediate shuffle files kept on disk (spark.local.dir)
BROADCAST hint syntax (SQL and DataFrame) and spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold default 10485760 (10 MB), -1 disables
spark.sql.shuffle.partitions default 200 (number of partitions when shuffling for joins or aggregations)
AQE: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled default true; coalescePartitions.enabled default true; advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes 64 MB
AQE skew join: skewJoin.enabled default true; splits (and replicates if needed) skewed partitions in sort-merge join
AQE converts sort-merge join to broadcast hash join when runtime stats of a join side are below the threshold
RDD HashPartitioner: getPartition = Utils.nonNegativeMod(key.hashCode, numPartitions) (Spark v4.2.0 source)
Spark SQL HashPartitioning: partitionIdExpression = Pmod(Murmur3Hash(expressions), numPartitions); rows with equal key values go to the same partition (Spark v4.2.0 source)

canBroadcastBySize: plan.stats.sizeInBytes >= 0 && sizeInBytes <= autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (inclusive, based on size statistics/estimates; adaptive threshold for runtime stats) (Spark v4.2.0 source)
ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator: local and host-local blocks are read without a remote fetch; zero-sized blocks are excluded from fetching (Spark v4.2.0 source)

on_screen_text: Usually copied across executors and machines

Show P0/P1/P2 with the 9 orders; A, B, C scattered in every partition. SQL panel shows code_blocks[0].

on_screen_text: Map side: route rows by key
scenes.beat: Each map task tags each row with a target partition, sorts by target and writes one file. Assignments are illustrative, no real hash values.

on_screen_text: Each task pulls its blocks from the map outputs
scenes.beat: R0 pulls all A rows from P0, P1, P2; R1 pulls B; R2 pulls C. Arrows fan in across machines.

on_screen_text: Now each key is in one place
scenes.beat: Reduce partitions sum their rows; result table appears matching the SQL output.

on_screen_text: Spills add more disk and GC
scenes.beat: Three cost badges light up on the arrows from s5; a spill icon drops to disk.

on_screen_text: Small side? Broadcast it (auto ≤ 10 MB by default)
scenes.beat: Broadcast: small table (by estimated size) copied to every executor, big side stays put. Then tiny partitions merge, one fat partition splits.
